Signing in with OpenID Connect
OpenID is a standardized way to let you log into websites using an account from another service, like Google or Authelia, to verify your identity.

When OpenID is activated, the password-based authentication in Trilium is replaced with a button that connects using your provider. This means that the configuration of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Multi-factor authentication with TOTP__TRILIUM_PH_1__ no longer takes effect, since your provider has to handle any multi-factor authentication.

Those images keep their address on the original website: Trilium tries to download them once more if __TRILIUM_PH_0__Download images automatically__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is enabled in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Media__TRILIUM_PH_5__, and otherwise the note shows them from the website for as long as it serves them.
units.context: Web Clipper > Configuration > When a clipping fails

units.source: The notification is shown on the page itself, so it does not appear on pages where extensions cannot run (such as the browser's own settings pages, the extension stores and Firefox's PDF viewer). A clipping saved from the popup on such a page still reports in the popup.
units.context: Web Clipper > Configuration > When a clipping fails

Backup
Trilium supports simple backup scheme where it saves copy of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ on these events:
once a day
once a week
once a month
before DB migration to newer version

So in total you'll have at most 4 backups from different points in time which should protect you from various problems. These backups are stored by default in __TRILIUM_PH_0__ directory placed in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__data directory__TRILIUM_PH_2__.
This is only very basic backup solution, and you're encouraged to add some better backup solution - e.g. backing up the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to cloud / different computer etc.
Note that __TRILIUM_PH_0__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_1__ provides also some backup capabilities by its nature of distributing the data to other computers.

The backup will be saved as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Existing backups__TRILIUM_PH_2__ list, where you can download it.

Tree Settings__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Click the tree icon in the tree toolbar to open the tree settings popup. Each option takes effect as soon as it is changed:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Display density__TRILIUM_PH_1__: __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relaxed__TRILIUM_PH_3__ (default) or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Dense__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Dense rows are shorter, so more notes fit on the screen. This setting is not synchronized, so each device keeps its own.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Hide archived notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When enabled, archived notes are not shown in the tree.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Automatically collapse notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When enabled, notes are collapsed after a period of inactivity to keep the tree tidy.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Follow active note__TRILIUM_PH_1__: When enabled (default), the tree automatically scrolls and expands parent nodes to keep the currently active note visible. When disabled, the tree is fully detached from navigation — only the background highlight of the active note is updated, but the tree viewport and its expanded/collapsed state are never changed by navigation. Use the crosshair button to manually jump the tree to the active note at any time.

The icon of each item indicates whether it's a __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) or a __TRILIUM_PH_3__relation__TRILIUM_PH_4__ (__TRILIUM_PH_5__, link to another note).

Interaction:
Clicking on the item (apart from the value and links) reveals a dedicated popup where the name, value and __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_1__ can be defined.
The value of the attributes can be edited in-place:
The input box follows the type defined in a corresponding label definition (date, color, dropdown, numbers), as well as for system attributes that have a specific type (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__).
For labels, clicking on the value edits its in-place.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to confirm or click outside the input box, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to dismiss.
For multi-line text, __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_3__ confirms whereas __TRILIUM_PH_4__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_5__ creates a newline.

For labels without a value, a value can be added by clicking on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__No value__TRILIUM_PH_1__ text which appears while the mouse is hovered on the item.
For relations, there is a dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button instead.

An attribute can be deleted by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to its right, which only appears while hovered. A confirmation screen is displayed first to ensure the attribute is not accidentally deleted.
Attributes can be added in two ways:
A new label, relation or attribute definition can be added from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_2__. This shows the full detail popup.
To quickly add a label or a relation directly from the sidebar, click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add attribute__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) item at the end of the list.

The name field will be focused first. By default, a label will be created instead but it can be toggled to a relation by typing __TRILIUM_PH_0__~__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon (similarly, typing __TRILIUM_PH_3__ will switch back to a label instead of a relation).

Clicking outside the editor will also create the attribute, but only if a name is specified.
Inherited attributes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Inherited labels or relations are shown in the same fashion as the owned ones.
The only differences are:
To the right of the inherited attribute there is a link to the note where the attribute comes from, as well as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon to indicate that it's inheritable.
Clicking on an inherited attribute will reveal the same popup as owned attributes, but it is not editable. To edit it, first navigate to the note where the attribute is defined.

For attribute definition (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__):
The icon indicates the type of the attribute (text, number).
If an attribute is promoted, it has a small __TRILIUM_PH_0__ chevron icon overlaid on top of it.

Both kinds of definitions can also be added from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

Multiple attributes can be selected in order to copy or delete them together:

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button, which copies the selected attributes.

On mobile, the right sidebar is replaced by the note panel, which opens as a sheet at the bottom of the screen from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button beside the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_2__.

units.source: Content width
Some note types (such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and saved search) intentionally limit the width of the content.

This might appear surprising at first, but the idea is to make text fit well on wider screens without appearing distorted. This is especially the case if the document contains __TRILIUM_PH_0__Images__TRILIUM_PH_1__, tables or other width-dependent elements.
Configuring the content width and alignment__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.source: The content width is expressed in pixels and can be changed from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Appearance__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Content Width__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and adjusting the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Max content width__TRILIUM_PH_7__ section.
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.source: To effectively disable the content width limitation, simply set the width to a value larger than your screen size (e.g. 9999).
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.source: By default, the content is aligned to the left, but it can be centered horizontally by checking __TRILIUM_PH_0__Keep content centered__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the same section as the content width.
units.context: Content width > Configuring the content width and alignment

units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: Since v0.107.0, a single table can also be made wider than the content width, in which case it scrolls sideways. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Tables__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Content width > Adjusting at note level

units.source: Some __TRILIUM_PH_0__note types__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are full width by default, such as the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__. In that case the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_5__ toggle will not be displayed and the label will have no effect.

units.source: Attachments

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in Trilium can __TRILIUM_PH_2__own__TRILIUM_PH_3__ one or more attachments, which can be either images or files. These attachments can be displayed or linked within the note that owns them.

This can be especially useful to include dependencies for your __TRILIUM_PH_0__scripts__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The __TRILIUM_PH_2__Weight Tracker__TRILIUM_PH_3__ shows how to use __TRILIUM_PH_4__chartjs__TRILIUM_PH_5__ which is attached to the script note.

Each note exclusively owns its attachments, meaning attachments cannot be shared or linked from one note to another. If an attachment link is copied to a different note, the attachment itself is duplicated, and the copies are managed independently thereafter.

Attachments, especially image files, are the recommended method for embedding visuals in notes. It is important to link image attachments within the text of the owning note; otherwise, they will be automatically deleted after a configurable timeout period if not referenced.
Types of attachments__TRILIUM_PH_0__
There are two different types of attachment:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__User content__TRILIUM_PH_1__, representing files or images that are uploaded and part of the content of the note.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__System attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which are used internally by Trilium and can be of multiple types, including:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to store information about views such as the column information for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Icons and cover images for __TRILIUM_PH_0__Link Previews__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Debug information for some importers such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Microsoft OneNote__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (only if the debug flag was enabled at import time).
The transcript of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Meeting transcription__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which is also shown above the note's content.

The SVG picture of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note (__TRILIUM_PH_2__), and of each drawing canvas in a text note (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Drawing canvases__TRILIUM_PH_4__ in __TRILIUM_PH_5__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_6__), used for previews and shared pages.
The system attachments are displayed at the end of the attachments list, in a dedicated section (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Generated by Trilium__TRILIUM_PH_1__).
Uploading attachments__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_2__ item of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ opens the list of the note's attachments.
To upload files as attachments, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Upload attachments__TRILIUM_PH_1__ at the top of the list and select one or more files.

Alternatively, drag one or more files from the file explorer and drop them anywhere on the list. Pictures are compressed if __TRILIUM_PH_0__Automatic image compression__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is enabled in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Media__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
Attaching files from a text note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: To attach files to a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note and embed them in its content, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_6__, choose __TRILIUM_PH_7__Attach and embed file__TRILIUM_PH_8__ and select one or more files (see __TRILIUM_PH_9__Embedding an attachment__TRILIUM_PH_10__ below). The same menu offers __TRILIUM_PH_11__Image__TRILIUM_PH_12__, which inserts pictures (see __TRILIUM_PH_13__Images__TRILIUM_PH_14__), and __TRILIUM_PH_15__Attach file as a link__TRILIUM_PH_16__, which links the files instead. Both file actions are also available as __TRILIUM_PH_17__Attach file as a link__TRILIUM_PH_18__ and __TRILIUM_PH_19__Attach and embed file__TRILIUM_PH_20__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_21__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_22__. On a phone, the menu also offers __TRILIUM_PH_23__Camera__TRILIUM_PH_24__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_25__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_26__).
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: When files are attached as links:
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Each file becomes an attachment of the note, and a link to it is inserted at the cursor. Several files produce several links, separated by a space.
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: While a file uploads, its link shows the file name and a toast shows the progress.
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Pictures appear as links rather than images, and are attached exactly as they are, without being compressed. To display a picture in the text, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Image__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the same menu instead (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Images__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Dragging a file that is not a picture from the file explorer onto the text also attaches it and inserts a link to it.
units.context: Attachments > Attaching files from a text note

units.source: Acting on an attachment link__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Attachments > Acting on an attachment link

units.source: Right-clicking a link to an attachment shows the ways to open it, followed by actions on the attachment: opening it externally, downloading it, uploading a new revision, renaming or deleting it, and converting it into a note. In a text note being edited, the same entries are in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu of the popup of the link, which right-clicking the link opens. The popup also has a __TRILIUM_PH_3__ __TRILIUM_PH_4__Download__TRILIUM_PH_5__ button.
units.context: Attachments > Acting on an attachment link

units.source: Links follow changes to their attachment: renaming it updates the title they show, and deleting it removes them from the text notes open for editing at that moment. Converting it into a note turns its links into links to the new note.
units.context: Attachments > Acting on an attachment link

units.source: Embedding an attachment__TRILIUM_PH_0__

An attachment can be shown in the text instead of linked, the way __TRILIUM_PH_0__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows a note: a picture is displayed, a PDF, a video or a document is previewed, a code or text file is shown with syntax highlighting, and a Markdown file such as a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ file is shown rendered. An embedded code file can also be edited in place (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Editing an include in place__TRILIUM_PH_4__ in __TRILIUM_PH_5__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_6__), and an embedded Markdown file shows its source, its rendering or both, as an included Markdown note does (see __TRILIUM_PH_7__Included Markdown__TRILIUM_PH_8__ there).

To attach files and embed them straight away, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button and choose __TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach and embed file__TRILIUM_PH_4__. Each file gets an embed of its own, which shows the file name while the file uploads.
To embed an attachment that is already linked, right-click a link to it in a text note being edited and select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Convert link to an embed__TRILIUM_PH_1__, near the end of the menu.

A drawing canvas, inserted with __TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__Drawing canvas__TRILIUM_PH_2__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_3____TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_5__ menu, is an embed of a __TRILIUM_PH_6__ attachment that can be drawn on in place. An attached Excalidraw file (__TRILIUM_PH_7__) is embedded as a drawing canvas too (see __TRILIUM_PH_8__Drawing canvases__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in __TRILIUM_PH_10__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_11__).

An embed gets the box size that suits the attachment, as a new included note does (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Box sizes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ there). To change its size, select the embed and use the box size menu in its toolbar, or the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Size__TRILIUM_PH_3__ submenu of its __TRILIUM_PH_4____TRILIUM_PH_5__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_6__ menu. A __TRILIUM_PH_7__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_8__ embed can also be resized by dragging its handles, and an __TRILIUM_PH_9__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_10__ one in height (see __TRILIUM_PH_11__Resizing__TRILIUM_PH_12__ there). A __TRILIUM_PH_13__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_14__ embed can be placed at the left or the right of the note, with or without the text running beside it, from the __TRILIUM_PH_15__Position__TRILIUM_PH_16__ submenu of its menu (see __TRILIUM_PH_17__Positioning__TRILIUM_PH_18__ there).
An embed can have a caption, as an included note can (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Caption__TRILIUM_PH_1__ there).

To show only the attachment, turn off __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the embed's __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_4__ menu, as for an included note (see __TRILIUM_PH_5__Title__TRILIUM_PH_6__ there).
To open the attachment in a new tab, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (__TRILIUM_PH_1__Open in new tab)__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the end of the embed's title.

An embed of size __TRILIUM_PH_0__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_1__ shows only the title of the attachment and its size, in a single row, whatever the attachment is: a drawing canvas or a video shows nothing of its content there. Its buttons are __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Open externally__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5____TRILIUM_PH_6__Download__TRILIUM_PH_7__. An audio file at __TRILIUM_PH_8__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_9__ is a row of player controls instead, without its title until __TRILIUM_PH_10__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_11__ is turned on.

To show an embed of size __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Full__TRILIUM_PH_3__ on the whole screen, press the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ (__TRILIUM_PH_5__Fullscreen)__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button at the end of its title. To return, press __TRILIUM_PH_7__ (__TRILIUM_PH_8__Exit fullscreen)__TRILIUM_PH_9__ in the top-right corner, or __TRILIUM_PH_10__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_11__.

To turn the embed back into a link, choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__Convert to link__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the menu that right-clicking the title row of the embed or pressing its __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button opens. It is in the last group, after __TRILIUM_PH_5____TRILIUM_PH_6__Delete block__TRILIUM_PH_7__, which removes the embed from the note, and __TRILIUM_PH_8____TRILIUM_PH_9__Delete attachment...__TRILIUM_PH_10__, which deletes the attachment itself. __TRILIUM_PH_11____TRILIUM_PH_12__Convert attachment into note...__TRILIUM_PH_13__ follows it.

An embed follows its attachment like a link does. Converting the attachment into a note turns the embed into an included note. In a __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared note__TRILIUM_PH_1__, an embedded picture is displayed with its caption, a drawing canvas as a picture of the drawing, a video or audio file in the browser's player, and any other attachment, or a picture in a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_3__ embed, appears as a link to download it.
Converting notes to attachments__TRILIUM_PH_0__
__TRILIUM_PH_0__File__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes can be easily converted to attachments of the parent note.
To do so:
For a single note, press the context menu from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Convert into attachment__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
For multiple notes, select the given notes in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, right click → Advanced → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Convert to attachment…__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Attachment previews__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Branch prefix

Since a single note can appear into multiple places in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ via a process called __TRILIUM_PH_2__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__, it's recommended to choose a generalized name that fits into all locations instead of something more specific to avoid confusion.
In some cases this isn't possible so Trilium provides "branch prefixes", which is shown before the note name in the tree and as such provides a specific kind of context.
The prefix is location-specific, so it's displayed only in the note tree.
You can view the list of all available clones:
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Status bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, by looking for the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon.
In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Connections tab__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Right Sidebar__TRILIUM_PH_3__, by looking at the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note paths__TRILIUM_PH_5__ section.

In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__, on desktop and on mobile, the title of a cloned note is followed by a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ icon, to easily see that the note is also placed into some other location. A shared note is followed by a __TRILIUM_PH_3__ icon in the same way.

Protected Notes

Trilium is designed to store a wide variety of data, including sensitive information such as personal journals, credentials, or confidential documents. To safeguard this type of content, Trilium offers the option to protect notes, which involves the following measures:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Encryption:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Protected notes are encrypted using a key derived from your password. This ensures that without the correct password, protected notes remain indecipherable. Even if someone gains access to your Trilium __TRILIUM_PH_2__database__TRILIUM_PH_3__, they won't be able to read your encrypted notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Time-limited access:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ To access protected notes, you must first enter your password, which decrypts the note for reading and writing. However, after a specified period of inactivity (10 minutes by default), the note is unloaded from memory, requiring you to re-enter your password to access it again.

The session timeout is extended automatically while you're interacting with the protected note, so if you're actively editing, the session remains open. However, if you switch to an unprotected note, the session timer starts, and the session expires after 10 minutes of inactivity unless you return to the protected notes.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Protection scope:__TRILIUM_PH_1__ Protected notes ensure the confidentiality of their content and partially their integrity. While unauthorized users cannot read or edit protected notes, they can still delete or move them outside of the protected session.
Using Protected Notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
By default, notes are unprotected. To protect a note, simply click on the shield icon next to the note's title, as shown here:
What is Encrypted?__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Trilium encrypts the data within protected notes but not their metadata. Specifically:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Encrypted:__TRILIUM_PH_1__
Note title
Note content
Images
File attachments
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Not encrypted:__TRILIUM_PH_1__
Note structure (i.e., it remains visible that there are protected notes)
Metadata, such as the last modified date
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__
Encryption Details__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The following steps outline how encryption and decryption work in Trilium:
The user enters a password.
The password is passed through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__scrypt__TRILIUM_PH_1__ algorithm along with a "password verification" __TRILIUM_PH_2__salt__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to confirm that the password is correct.
The password is then processed again through scrypt with an "encryption" salt, which generates a hash.
Scrypt is used for __TRILIUM_PH_0__key stretching__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to make the password harder to guess.
The generated hash is used to decrypt the actual __TRILIUM_PH_0__data encryption key__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The data encryption key is encrypted using __TRILIUM_PH_0__AES-128__TRILIUM_PH_1__ with a random __TRILIUM_PH_2__IV__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

The data encryption key is randomly generated during the __TRILIUM_PH_0__database__TRILIUM_PH_1__ initialization and remains constant throughout the document’s lifetime. When the password is changed, only this key is re-encrypted.
The data encryption key is then used to decrypt the actual content of the note, including its title and body.
The encryption algorithm used is AES-128 with __TRILIUM_PH_0__CBC mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__, where a unique IV is generated for each encryption operation and stored with the cipher text.
Sharing Protected Notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Protected notes cannot be shared in the same way as regular notes. Their encryption ensures that only authorized users with the correct password can access them.
Going to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note revisions…__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Save revision__TRILIUM_PH_5__ (__TRILIUM_PH_6__).

units.source: Read-Only Notes

Some note types such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Code__TRILIUM_PH_3__ notes and even some of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_5__ can be set to read-only. Automatic read-only mode__TRILIUM_PH_0__

For optimization purposes, Trilium will automatically set very large notes to read-only. Displaying such lengthy notes in editing mode can slow down performance, especially when editing is unnecessary.
This behavior can be disabled on a per-note basis, by following the instructions of the next section.

In addition, it's possible to change the number of characters at which the automatic read-only mode will trigger in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ by going to the options for __TRILIUM_PH_2__Text Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Code Notes__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

Notes
Note is a central entity in Trilium. Main attributes of note are __TRILIUM_PH_0__title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and content.
Note types__TRILIUM_PH_0__

The main note type is a rich-text note type called __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__. For diagrams and drawing there is __TRILIUM_PH_2__Canvas__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Mermaid Diagrams__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

There are also more complex note types such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Render Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ that usually go hand-in-hand with __TRILIUM_PH_4__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

In Trilium there's no specific "folder" note type. Any note can have children and thus be a folder. To make a note that only shows its children, like a folder in other applications, use a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__List View__TRILIUM_PH_3__ collection. See also __TRILIUM_PH_4__FAQ__TRILIUM_PH_5__.
Root note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
There's one special note called "root note" which is root of the note tree. All other notes are placed below it in the structure.
Tree structure__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Importantly, note itself doesn't carry information on its placement in note tree. See __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for details.

Tree structure of notes can resemble file system - but compared to that notes in Trilium can act as both file and directory - meaning that note can both have its own content and have children. "Leaf note" is a note which doesn't have any children.
Deleting / undeleting notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
When you delete a note in Trilium, it is actually only marked for deletion (soft-delete) - the actual content, title, attributes etc. are not deleted, only hidden.

Within (by default) 7 days, it is possible to undelete these soft-deleted notes - open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Recent Changes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog, and you will see a list of all modified notes including the deleted ones. Notes available for undeletion have a link to do so. This is kind of "trash can" functionality known from e.g. Windows.

Clicking an undelete will recover the note, its content and attributes - note should be just as before being deleted. This action will also undelete note's children which have been deleted in the same action.

To be able to undelete a note, it is necessary that deleted note's parent must be undeleted (otherwise there's no place where we can undelete it to). This might become a problem when you delete more notes in succession - the solution is then undelete in the reverse order of your deletion.
Note Navigation
One of the Trilium's goals is to provide fast and comfortable navigation between notes.
Backwards and forward__TRILIUM_PH_0__

To move back and forward in the history of viewed notes, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__←__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Alt__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__→__TRILIUM_PH_7__, or use the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ and __TRILIUM_PH_9__ buttons to the left of the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_11__.
This works identically to browser backwards / forwards, it's actually using built-in browser support for this.

To go several notes back or forward at once, right-click one of the buttons or press and hold it. The back button lists the notes before the current one and the forward button the notes after it, the nearest first. Each entry shows the note's title, with the path of its parent notes at the end of the row. Selecting a note goes straight to it.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Go to Previous Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Go to Next Note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ launchers of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_5__ list the same notes, below the launch bar's own items.

units.source: Search

Note search enables you to find notes by searching for text in the title, content, or __TRILIUM_PH_0__attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the notes. You also have the option to save your searches, which will create a special search note which is visible on your navigation tree and contains the search results as sub-items.
Types of search__TRILIUM_PH_0__
There are multiple types of searches, all using the same search mechanism and query language:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ which can be found in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for small one-off searches.
The results are shown in a popup and it has an infinite scroll.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Full search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is the more advanced search mechanism.
The results are displayed in a separate page and it has multiple advanced features (search script, fast search, include archived notes, order by, limit).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as adding a label/relation can be applied to the results.
The results are paginated and they can be displayed in any __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view (e.g. grid, list, calendar, table).
Some __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as board view have a dedicated search bar which applies to that collection.
In this case, the results are displayed directly in the collection instead of a popup and they are limited to the collection but the query language remains the same.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is a similar concept but it's mainly used to search for notes by title, not by content. Nevertheless, it also features a way to search in full text if the results are unsatisfactory.
Accessing the search__TRILIUM_PH_0__
From the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for the dedicated __TRILIUM_PH_2__ search button.

To limit the search to a note and its children, select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search in subtree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) from the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Note tree contextual menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ or press __TRILIUM_PH_5__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_6__+__TRILIUM_PH_7__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_8__+__TRILIUM_PH_9__S__TRILIUM_PH_10__.

Go to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to & command palette__TRILIUM_PH_1__, look for something then press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show in full search__TRILIUM_PH_3__ below the results (or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_5__+__TRILIUM_PH_6__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_7__).
Interaction__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To search for notes, click on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ icon in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_2__ or press the keyboard __TRILIUM_PH_3__shortcut__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
Set the text to search for in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search string__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field.
Apart from searching for words literally, there is also the possibility to search for attributes or properties of notes.
See the examples below for more information.
To limit the search to a note and its sub-children, set a note in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ancestor__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
This value is also pre-filled if the search is triggered from a __TRILIUM_PH_0__hoisted note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or a __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspace__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To search the entire database, keep the value empty.

To limit the search to only a few levels of hierarchy (e.g. look in sub-children but not in sub-sub-children of a note), set the __TRILIUM_PH_0__depth__TRILIUM_PH_1__ field to one of the provided values.
In addition to that, the search can be configured via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add search option__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu, as described in the follow-up section.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) to trigger the search. The results are displayed below the search configuration pane.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search & Execute actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) entry in the menu beside __TRILIUM_PH_3__Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__ is only relevant if at least one action has been added (as described in the section below).

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Save to note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) entry in the same menu will create a new note with the search configuration. For more information, see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Saved Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__.
Features__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Autocomplete__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To help with the syntax, Trilium offers an autocomplete functionality which can be triggered by pressing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__Space__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

Some suggestions also open on their own as you type: label and relation names after __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__, fields after __TRILIUM_PH_2__, operators, values, and notes after __TRILIUM_PH_3__. This is especially useful for queries that make use of the note ID such as searching by template: __TRILIUM_PH_0__
Syntax highlighting__TRILIUM_PH_0__
The search input features syntax highlighting, making recognized fields such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and operators like __TRILIUM_PH_1__ stand out.
This feature allows writing a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note that will handle the search on its own.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Fast search
The search will not look into the content of the notes, but it will still look into note titles and attributes, relations (based on the search query).
This method can speed up the search considerably for large __TRILIUM_PH_0__databases__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__ Order by
Allows changing the criteria for ordering the results, for example to order by creation date or alphabetically instead of by relevancy (default).
It's also possible to change the order (ascending or descending) of the results.

Limits the results to a given maximum.
This can help if the number of results would otherwise be high, at the cost of not being able to view all the results.

The same menu ends with a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Bulk actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section for applying changes such as adding a label or a relation to the matched notes. Its groups—__TRILIUM_PH_2__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_5__, __TRILIUM_PH_6__Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Other__TRILIUM_PH_9__—each open a list of the actions in the corresponding group of the __TRILIUM_PH_10__Bulk Actions__TRILIUM_PH_11__ dialog, which is an alternative for operating directly with notes within the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_13__. Viewing search results__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Results appear below the search pane, by default in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view. Each result is drawn as a __TRILIUM_PH_2__snippet card__TRILIUM_PH_3__ with the note title, the path to it, a short excerpt of the matching text, and the attributes that matched. The excerpt of a code note keeps its indentation and is shown in the code font.

To show the results as a plain note list instead, choose __TRILIUM_PH_0__List__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_3__ bar. The __TRILIUM_PH_4__List__TRILIUM_PH_5__ view shows one row per note, with the note's title and content preview.
The search will also highlight the words from the title or content that matched:
With a solid underlined green for a direct match;
With a dotted underline orange for a partial match (matched by the fuzzy search).
In addition, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_1__ view offers:
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__total number of results__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is always shown, so you can immediately tell how broad a query is.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__page-size selector__TRILIUM_PH_1__ lets you choose how many results to display per page. Your choice is remembered and synced across your devices (stored in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ option), so you do not have to reset it on every device.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Clicking a result's title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ opens the note and jumps straight to the first match. The in-note find bar opens pre-filled with the first word of your search, so you can step through its matches with the find controls. To have the find bar look for a whole phrase instead, put the phrase in quotes in the search, e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_2__. In read-only notes, the other words of the search are highlighted as well. The excerpt and attributes can be selected without opening the note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Open all results in new tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (__TRILIUM_PH_2__, the button above the results) opens every result in a tab of its own, up to 50. Each tab opens on its first match with the find bar pre-filled, as when clicking a result.
If a match is inside a __TRILIUM_PH_0__collapsed section__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (for example a folded heading), that section is expanded automatically so the match is visible.

When the excerpt is cut short, a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show more__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button expands the card to the note's full content, with the search terms highlighted. __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show less__TRILIUM_PH_3__ returns to the excerpt.

A saved search can also be __TRILIUM_PH_0__printed or exported as PDF__TRILIUM_PH_1__ from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Print/export to PDF…__TRILIUM_PH_3__ item of the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_5__, in either __TRILIUM_PH_6__Search preview__TRILIUM_PH_7__ or __TRILIUM_PH_8__List__TRILIUM_PH_9__ view. The results are laid out as a list, as they stand when printing starts.

Bookmarks
Frequently used notes can be bookmarked, which will make them appear in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for easy access.
Configuring the launch bar__TRILIUM_PH_0__

If bookmarks don't appear in the launch bar, then most likely the bookmark section has been hidden. Go to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ configuration from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and ensure __TRILIUM_PH_4__Bookmarks__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is in the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Visible Launchers__TRILIUM_PH_7__ section.
Bookmark folder__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Space in the left panel is limited, and you might want to bookmark many items. One possible solution is to bookmark a folder, so it shows its children:

To do this, bookmark a folder, then right click its button in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and check __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show as a folder__TRILIUM_PH_3__. The button then opens a menu instead of the note itself: the note is at the top, followed by its children. Uncheck __TRILIUM_PH_4__Show as a folder__TRILIUM_PH_5__ to turn it back into a regular bookmark.

A child that has children of its own shows an arrow at the end of its row. Click the arrow to list its children in a submenu, or click the rest of the row to open the note. Submenus nest up to four levels deep. A menu that lists more than 15 children shows a filter field above them: type part of a title to list only the notes that match. A note whose subtree is hidden (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Hiding the subtree__TRILIUM_PH_1__) doesn't list its children here either.

The notes in the menu open the way links do: a middle click or __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+click opens a note in a new tab, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shift__TRILIUM_PH_3__+click opens it in a new window, and a right click lists the other places it can be opened in.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Show as a folder__TRILIUM_PH_1__ assigns the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ label to the note, so adding the label by hand works as well. Because the label belongs to the note, a note that is both bookmarked and dropped onto the launch bar shows its children in both places.

units.source: Mobile__TRILIUM_PH_0__

On mobile, bookmarks are only displayed starting with v0.102.0. Because of the more constrained screen size, the bookmarks are grouped under a single icon instead of displaying them as separate icons.

When pressed, a menu will appear listing all the bookmarks. Bookmark folders are also supported and will appear as submenus. Each submenu starts with its own note, so a note with children can be opened as well as browsed.

On a phone, the bookmarks are also listed at the top of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while it shows the root of a tab that is not hoisted, below the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Tap a bookmark to open it, or, for one with children, to list them, as with the other notes of the tree.
Note Hoisting
Hoisting is a standard outliner feature which allows you to focus on (or "zoom into") a specific note and its subtree by hiding all parent and sibling notes. Demo:
In addition to showing only this subtree, this also narrows both full text search and __TRILIUM_PH_0__“jump to note”__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to just notes present in hoisted subtree.

units.source: Quick edit
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_1__ provides an alternative to the standard tab-based navigation and editing.

Instead of clicking on a note which switches the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to the newly selected note, or navigating between two different __TRILIUM_PH_2__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_3__, the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_5__ feature opens as a popup window that can be easily dismissed.

This feature is also well integrated with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ such as the calendar view, which makes it easy to edit entries without having to go back and forth between the child note and the calendar.
Feature highlights__TRILIUM_PH_0__
All note types are supported, including __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Note that the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note List__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will not be displayed, except for notes of type __TRILIUM_PH_2__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
For __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes, depending on user preference, both the floating and classic editors are supported. See __TRILIUM_PH_2__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
The title and the note and the icon are editable, just like a normal tab.
The note's actions and its menu are shown in the header of the popup, as in the title row of a tab.
When other notes link to the note, a button with a link icon lists the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Backlinks__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Pressing one opens that note in the popup.
The menu items that only work in a tab are not shown: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note map__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Full width__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__Convert into attachment__TRILIUM_PH_5__.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Find__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the menu, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__+__TRILIUM_PH_4__F__TRILIUM_PH_5__ on the desktop application, opens the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Search in note__TRILIUM_PH_7__ bar at the bottom of the popup. It searches the note in the popup, not the note in the tab behind it.
A help page opened from the popup, such as through the help button of the note type, opens in a second popup on top of it. Closing that popup returns to the note being edited.
The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ are also displayed.

This integrates well with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collections__TRILIUM_PH_1__ where there are predefined attributes such as the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Start date__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and __TRILIUM_PH_4__End date__TRILIUM_PH_5__, allowing for easy editing.
Workspaces

Workspace is a concept built up on top of __TRILIUM_PH_0__note hoisting__TRILIUM_PH_1__. It is based on the idea that a user has several distinct spheres of interest. An example might be "Personal" and "Work", these two spheres are quite distinct and don't interact together. When I focus on Work, I don't really care about personal notes.
So far workspace consists of these features:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__note hoisting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ - you can "zoom" into a workspace subtree to focus only on the relevant notes
easy entering of workspace:
opening a workspace in a new tab: right-click the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button of the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Tabs__TRILIUM_PH_2__ bar and select the workspace.

on a phone, the workspaces are listed at the top of the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ while it shows the root of a tab that is not hoisted, such as a new tab. Tap one to enter it, and tap the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the top of the workspace's tree to leave it.

Themes
Default Themes__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Trilium comes with a couple pre-installed color themes, with the default being a light theme. To switch to a dark theme or any other available theme, navigate to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ Options menu (accessible via the app icon in the top-left corner), select the Appearance tab, and choose your preferred theme. The __TRILIUM_PH_1__Theme__TRILIUM_PH_2__ submenu of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_4__ switches the theme and the color scheme as well.

While a dark theme is active, Trilium asks the Dark Reader browser extension not to darken the page a second time. Dark Reader still darkens the light themes. After switching from a dark theme to a light one, reload the page (__TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__R__TRILIUM_PH_3__) for Dark Reader to take effect again.

units.source: Tabs use the syntax of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Material for MkDocs__TRILIUM_PH_1__: each tab starts with a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ line, followed by its content indented by four spaces. Consecutive tabs form one tabs block, and __TRILIUM_PH_3__ starts a new block right after another one:

Tabs can be nested by indenting the inner tabs inside the content of a tab. A tab title is plain text, so its formatting is not kept on export. For how tabs blocks work in a text note, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Content tabs__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
Wikilinks__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Basic support for wikilinks has been added in v0.96.0:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ will look for the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ file in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory and turn it into an internal link.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__ will look for the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ file in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ directory and turn it into an image.
This feature is import-only, which means that it will turn wikilinks into Trilium-compatible syntax, but it will not export Trilium Notes into Markdown files with this syntax.

The path to pages in wikilinks is resolved relatively to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__import root__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and not the current directory of the note. This is to be inline with other platforms that use wikilinks such as SilverBullet.
The root path of the import is determined as follows:
If there is a single directory within the archive at root level, then that directory is considered the root.
If there are multiple files & directories at root level, then the archive root (containing all of these items) is considered the root.

Maximum import size__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Versions prior to v0.104.0 had an upload limit of 250 MiB that could be bypassed via a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ environment variable; with v0.104.0 this limit was removed.

Nevertheless, there is still a limit for the maximum size of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__single item__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (whether it's a __TRILIUM_PH_2__File__TRILIUM_PH_3__, an __TRILIUM_PH_4__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or even a __TRILIUM_PH_6__Text__TRILIUM_PH_7__ note). The limit is approximately 374 MiB and it's determined by the __TRILIUM_PH_8__Synchronization__TRILIUM_PH_9__ protocol. Attempts to import such large files will be refused.
During large imports or exports, memory consumption might spike but it will remain somewhere around the 2 gigabyte mark. Tested with a 2.4 GB database with ~21k notes.
For the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Desktop Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__, there are two distinct import mechanisms:
A quick import, from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
The import dialog (via right click in the note tree → __TRILIUM_PH_0__Import into note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or from __TRILIUM_PH_2__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
When dealing with large files (multi-gigabyte), prefer using the import dialog as it has a special mechanism which makes sure that the file is read directly from disk rather than uploaded again.

Anchors

This feature used to be called __TRILIUM_PH_0__Bookmarks__TRILIUM_PH_1__ (as it is the official name in the editor we are using), but in order not to collide with the concept of __TRILIUM_PH_2__Bookmarks__TRILIUM_PH_3__, we have renamed it to __TRILIUM_PH_4__Anchors.__TRILIUM_PH_5__
Anchors allows creating __TRILIUM_PH_0__links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to a certain part of a note, such as referencing a particular heading or section within a note.
This feature was introduced in TriliumNext v0.94.0 and augmented in v0.103.0 to support linking across notes.
Interaction__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To create an anchor:
Place the cursor at the desired position where to place the anchor.
Look for the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_1__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_2__, and then press the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ button.
Alternatively, use __TRILIUM_PH_0__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and look for __TRILIUM_PH_2__anchor__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
To place a link to an anchor in the same note:
Place the cursor at the desired position of the link, or select the text to turn into a link.

Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__+__TRILIUM_PH_2__K__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ button in the __TRILIUM_PH_5__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_6__, then select __TRILIUM_PH_7__Heading / anchor__TRILIUM_PH_8__ at the top of the __TRILIUM_PH_9____TRILIUM_PH_10__Add link__TRILIUM_PH_11__ dialog__TRILIUM_PH_12__. Alternatively, choose __TRILIUM_PH_13__Link to a heading or anchor__TRILIUM_PH_14__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_15__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_16__, which opens the dialog on that page.
Under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Anchors__TRILIUM_PH_1__, click the desired anchor to check it. Optionally, type a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Link title__TRILIUM_PH_3__; without one, the link shows the anchor's name.
Press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enter__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert link__TRILIUM_PH_3__ to confirm.

Clicking a link to an anchor of the same note scrolls to the anchor and briefly highlights the block that holds it, in read-only notes and on shared pages. While editing, clicking the link shows its popup, whose __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to anchor__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button does the same, as do __TRILIUM_PH_2__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_3__+click and double-click.

Block quotes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
As the name suggests, block quotes can be useful to cite one or more paragraphs.

Inside the quote block, other block items can be inserted such as tables, images, or even other block quotes or admonitions.
Admonitions__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Admonitions are a way to highlight information to the reader. Other names for it include __TRILIUM_PH_0__call-outs__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__info/warning/alert boxes__TRILIUM_PH_3__.

units.source: Following a reference__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Clicking a block reference opens the note, scrolls to the referenced blocks and flashes them. If a referenced block was deleted, an error message is shown instead, along with the blocks of the range that still exist.

A link to blocks of the note it is in, such as a link to a heading, scrolls to them and flashes them without leaving the note, as a link within a web page does. This works in read-only notes and on shared pages too. While editing, clicking the link shows its popup: press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Jump to heading__TRILIUM_PH_1__ there, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Jump to block__TRILIUM_PH_3__ for other blocks.

units.source: Limitations__TRILIUM_PH_0__
References can be copied only from a note being edited, and not in the mobile layout.

Deleting a block breaks the references to it.
Content tabs

Content tabs group several titled panels of content into one block that shows a single panel at a time. They suit content that comes in variants (such as installation steps for each operating system or the same snippet in several programming languages).
A tabs block consists of:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__A single row of tab titles__TRILIUM_PH_1__, above the panel or, when the tabs are aligned at the bottom, below it. The title of the panel that is showing is highlighted.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__The panel of the active tab.__TRILIUM_PH_1__ A panel can hold any kind of content (including nested tabs blocks).

units.source: Extended code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Extended code blocks are experimental, and they change as they mature. To use them, turn on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Extended code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Options__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Experimental Options__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

An extended code block is a code block that is edited with the code editor of a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Code__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note, inside the text. It has the same syntax highlighting and code folding as a code note, and it suits longer pieces of code.

To insert one, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_2__ menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and choose __TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__Extended code block__TRILIUM_PH_7__, after __TRILIUM_PH_8__Columns__TRILIUM_PH_9__. It is also available as __TRILIUM_PH_10__Extended code block__TRILIUM_PH_11__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Slash Commands__TRILIUM_PH_13__.

A new block is empty and editable, in a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Full__TRILIUM_PH_1__ box, and takes the focus. Its language is the one set last on an extended code block, or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Plain text__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
A click places the cursor in the code, as in a code block. Over a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Small__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Medium__TRILIUM_PH_3__ box, the mouse wheel scrolls the code.

The block shows in a box like the one of an included code note, with the corners and the shadow of a code block. While the block is editable, its language shows in its top corner, as for a code block. While it is read-only, because __TRILIUM_PH_0__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is unchecked or the note is one of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Read-Only Notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__, that corner has a __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Copy to clipboard__TRILIUM_PH_6__ button instead, as a code block of a read-only note does.

Its toolbar has the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Change language mode__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Change tab width__TRILIUM_PH_3__ menus of an embedded code file, described in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Editing an include in place__TRILIUM_PH_5__ in __TRILIUM_PH_6__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_7__, and the __TRILIUM_PH_8__ __TRILIUM_PH_9__Copy to clipboard__TRILIUM_PH_10__ button, which copies the code as the one of a code block does. Its __TRILIUM_PH_11__ __TRILIUM_PH_12__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_13__ menu has __TRILIUM_PH_14__Editable__TRILIUM_PH_15__, which shows the code read-only once unchecked, the __TRILIUM_PH_16__Word wrap__TRILIUM_PH_17__ and __TRILIUM_PH_18__Line numbers__TRILIUM_PH_19__ submenus, the __TRILIUM_PH_20__Size__TRILIUM_PH_21__ submenu, with __TRILIUM_PH_22__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_23__, __TRILIUM_PH_24__Full__TRILIUM_PH_25__ and __TRILIUM_PH_26__Default__TRILIUM_PH_27__, the __TRILIUM_PH_28__Position__TRILIUM_PH_29__ submenu, and __TRILIUM_PH_30__ __TRILIUM_PH_31__Delete block__TRILIUM_PH_32__, which removes the block from the note.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Position__TRILIUM_PH_1__ submenu places the block as it places an include, described in __TRILIUM_PH_2__Positioning__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in __TRILIUM_PH_4__Include Note__TRILIUM_PH_5__: on lines of its own at the left, the center or the right, or at the left or the right with the text running beside it. Only a __TRILIUM_PH_6__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_7__ box can be placed, and it takes the full width of the note until it is resized narrower. In the mobile layout, a block with a position other than __TRILIUM_PH_8__Align center__TRILIUM_PH_9__ takes the full width.
The changes made in the block are part of the undo history of the text note.

The code stays in the note as a code block of its language. The Markdown export, __TRILIUM_PH_0__shared pages__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and printing show it as a code block, and copying it into another application pastes a code block. Pasted into a text note, it becomes an extended code block again, with its settings.

Turning __TRILIUM_PH_0__Extended code blocks__TRILIUM_PH_1__ off again removes them from the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert__TRILIUM_PH_3__ menu and the slash commands only: the extended code blocks already in notes keep working. A version of Trilium without this feature shows them as code blocks, and saves them back as code blocks, without their box size and other settings.

Format Painter

The Format Painter is a feature in text notes that allows users to copy the formatting of text (such as __TRILIUM_PH_0__bold__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__italic__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Strikethrough__TRILIUM_PH_5__, etc.) and apply it to other parts of the document. It helps maintain consistent formatting and accelerates the creation of rich content.
Usage Instructions__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Click the text that you want to copy the formatting from and use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Copy formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__ toolbar button (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) to copy the style. Then select the target text with your mouse, or click a word, to apply the formatting.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To copy the formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Place the cursor inside text with some formatting and click the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Copy formatting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ toolbar button. The mouse cursor changes to indicate the painter is armed.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To paint with the copied formatting__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Select the target text with your mouse. The formatting is applied when you release the button, and the painter disarms — the cursor returns to normal. Clicking or tapping a word applies it to the whole word.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__To paint a selection made otherwise__TRILIUM_PH_1__, such as with the keyboard or the selection handles of a touch screen: select the target text, then use the toolbar button again, which reads __TRILIUM_PH_2__Apply formatting__TRILIUM_PH_3__ once the selection has moved. On a phone, the formatting row stays open while the painter is armed, so the button stays in reach.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__To cancel without painting__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Click the toolbar button again before selecting other text, or press __TRILIUM_PH_2__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
Limitations__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Painting with block-level formatting (like headings or image styles) is not supported yet. This is because, in __TRILIUM_PH_0__CKEditor__TRILIUM_PH_1__, they are considered a part of the content rather than text formatting.
A click outside a word, such as between two spaces or at the end of a line, only primes the caret, so text you type there takes the copied formatting.
The painter is one-shot; each paint requires copying the formatting again.

Avoid using this feature just to simply make all text bigger. In that case it's generally better to adjust the font size for all notes in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or by zooming.

Clicking an image reference while __TRILIUM_PH_0__Ctrl__TRILIUM_PH_1__ is pressed will open the target note in a new tab.
Modifying the target note should also update the image reference. If that doesn't happen, consider __TRILIUM_PH_0__Refreshing the application__TRILIUM_PH_1__.

Images
Trilium supports storing and displaying images. Supported formats are PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP, AVIF and SVG.

An image can be uploaded in the form of note's __TRILIUM_PH_0__attachment__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or as a standalone __TRILIUM_PH_2__note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ placed into the __TRILIUM_PH_4__note tree__TRILIUM_PH_5__. Its reference can be copied into a text note, in order to display it in the text itself.
Uploading images__TRILIUM_PH_0__
To add an image to the note:
Simply drag it from file explorer onto the note editor inside Trilium and the image will be uploaded.

Alternatively, in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Formatting toolbar__TRILIUM_PH_1__, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button and select __TRILIUM_PH_5__Image__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
On the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Mobile Frontend__TRILIUM_PH_1__, the same menu also offers __TRILIUM_PH_2__Camera__TRILIUM_PH_3__, which takes a photo and inserts it.
You can also copy and paste an image from web (see section below).

Where the image goes depends on the cursor. In an empty paragraph, the image is displayed on a line of its own. In a list item, or after some text in a paragraph, the image is inserted __TRILIUM_PH_0__In line__TRILIUM_PH_1__, inside the text. To change it afterwards, use the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Image position__TRILIUM_PH_3__ button described in the alignment section below.

To link a picture instead of displaying it, attach it with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attach file as a link__TRILIUM_PH_1__, from the __TRILIUM_PH_2____TRILIUM_PH_3__Attach file__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button. See __TRILIUM_PH_5__Attachments__TRILIUM_PH_6__.
Clipboard & automatic download of images__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: Trilium has a special handling for images copied to and pasted from the clipboard.
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: For a mix of text and images, the images are downloaded automatically by the server (or desktop app, depending on what is being used).
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: This means that the image must be publicly accessible and reachable from wherever Trilium is running. Inaccessible images will end up as broken images.
units.context: Images > Clipboard & automatic download of images

units.source: If a single image is pasted into Trilium, it will prefer the image that comes in the clipboard. This makes it possible to copy images that Trilium would not otherwise be able to reach, such as Google Chat, Slack, etc.

units.source: In-editor AI assistant

The AI assistant works on the text you are already writing: select a passage and have it rewritten, translated or turned into a table, or ask for new content at the cursor. Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_0__AI chat__TRILIUM_PH_1__, it does not open a conversation window, the result is previewed in place and only enters the note when you accept it.
Requirements__TRILIUM_PH_0__

The assistant is only available once at least one provider is configured in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Options__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__AI / LLM__TRILIUM_PH_3__, with at least one model selected for it. Until then the toolbar entry is not shown at all.

units.source: Since v0.107.0, the box sizes were reworked: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Small__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__Medium__TRILIUM_PH_3__ are replaced by __TRILIUM_PH_4__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_5__. An include saved as __TRILIUM_PH_6__Small__TRILIUM_PH_7__ or __TRILIUM_PH_8__Medium__TRILIUM_PH_9__ by an earlier version opens as __TRILIUM_PH_10__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_11__, at the height it had.
A new include gets the size that suits what it shows:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for a note or an attachment that has no preview, such as a relation map or an archive, and for audio.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Full__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for a code note or a code file, such as a __TRILIUM_PH_2__, __TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__ attachment, and for an excerpt of the blocks of a text note.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for anything else.

The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Include note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog selects that size among its __TRILIUM_PH_2__Box size__TRILIUM_PH_3__ buttons once the note is picked, and you can choose another one there. To change the size later, select the include and use the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Box size__TRILIUM_PH_5__ menu in its toolbar, or the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Size__TRILIUM_PH_7__ submenu of its __TRILIUM_PH_8__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_9__ menu. Both have __TRILIUM_PH_10__Default__TRILIUM_PH_11__, which puts the include back at the size it started with, without a resized width or height; it is unavailable while the include is already there. For an included code or Markdown note and an embedded code or Markdown file, the __TRILIUM_PH_12__Box size__TRILIUM_PH_13__ menu is the __TRILIUM_PH_14__ button, whose tooltip names the current size.
Resizing__TRILIUM_PH_0__

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ include can be resized to any width and height, and an __TRILIUM_PH_2__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_3__ include in height. A __TRILIUM_PH_4__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_5__ or __TRILIUM_PH_6__Full__TRILIUM_PH_7__ include always fits its content.

To resize an include, select it and drag the handle in its bottom-right corner. To change only the width or only the height, drag the middle of its right or bottom edge instead, where a touch screen shows a handle too. In right-to-left text, the handle is in the bottom-left corner and the width changes from the left edge.
Resizing works with a mouse, a pen or a finger.
While the height changes, moving the handle near the top or the bottom of the note scrolls the note.

An include narrower than the note is centered, so changing its width moves both of its sides. An include aligned to the left or the right keeps that side in place and has its handles on the other side (see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Positioning__TRILIUM_PH_1__ below). Making an include as wide as the note returns it to the full width.
To cancel a resize, press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Esc__TRILIUM_PH_1__ before releasing the handle.
To reset the size, double-click the corner handle, or double-tap it on a touch screen. Double-clicking the right or bottom edge resets only the width or the height.

Choosing __TRILIUM_PH_0__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Full__TRILIUM_PH_3__ removes the resized width and height, and choosing __TRILIUM_PH_4__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_5__ removes the width, as it takes the full width of the note. __TRILIUM_PH_6__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_7__ keeps both, and __TRILIUM_PH_8__Default__TRILIUM_PH_9__ removes both.
While an __TRILIUM_PH_0__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ include is collapsed, it cannot be resized.
Positioning__TRILIUM_PH_0__
An include can sit on lines of its own or have the text wrap around it, as an __TRILIUM_PH_0__image__TRILIUM_PH_1__ can.

To change the position, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_1__ menu of the include in a note being edited (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Opening an included note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ below) and choose an entry of its __TRILIUM_PH_4__Position__TRILIUM_PH_5__ submenu:

Under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Break text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Align left__TRILIUM_PH_4__, __TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__Align center__TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__ __TRILIUM_PH_9__Align right__TRILIUM_PH_10__ place the include on lines of its own, at that side of the note. __TRILIUM_PH_11__Align center__TRILIUM_PH_12__ is the default.

Under __TRILIUM_PH_0__Wrap text__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__Align left__TRILIUM_PH_4__ and __TRILIUM_PH_5__ __TRILIUM_PH_6__Align right__TRILIUM_PH_7__ place the include at that side and let the text run beside it.

Only a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ include can be placed in the text. It takes the full width of the note until it is resized, so a new position shows once it is resized narrower (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Resizing__TRILIUM_PH_3__ above). An __TRILIUM_PH_4__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_5__ include takes the full width and offers the __TRILIUM_PH_6__Break text__TRILIUM_PH_7__ positions alone, which align the content inside its box. A __TRILIUM_PH_8__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_9__ or __TRILIUM_PH_10__Full__TRILIUM_PH_11__ include has no __TRILIUM_PH_12__Position__TRILIUM_PH_13__ submenu. A position is kept through a change of box size, and shows again once the include is __TRILIUM_PH_14__Resizable__TRILIUM_PH_15__.
In the mobile layout, an include with a position other than __TRILIUM_PH_0__Align center__TRILIUM_PH_1__ takes the full width, and only its height can be resized.
Caption__TRILIUM_PH_0__
An include can have a caption, shown centered at the bottom of its box. The caption is part of the text note, so it can be formatted like the rest of the text, for example in bold or with a link.

To add a caption, select the include, press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Toggle caption on__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in its toolbar and type the caption. While the cursor is in the caption, the include stays selected and keeps its toolbar.
To remove the caption, press the same button again. Pressing it once more brings back the text it had, as long as the note stays open.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_1__ include has no caption, unless it is an audio file. Switching an include to __TRILIUM_PH_2__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_3__ removes its caption, and switching it back to a larger size restores the caption, as long as the note stays open.
An __TRILIUM_PH_0__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_1__ include shows its caption under the title while the content is collapsed, and under the content once it is expanded.
Title__TRILIUM_PH_0__

The title row of an include links to the included note and holds its buttons. To show only the content, turn off __TRILIUM_PH_0__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ in the menu of the include, which right-clicking the title row or pressing its __TRILIUM_PH_2__ __TRILIUM_PH_3__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_4__ button opens (see __TRILIUM_PH_5__Opening an included note__TRILIUM_PH_6__ below).

While the title is hidden, select the include and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__More actions__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button in its toolbar to open the same menu, where turning on __TRILIUM_PH_3__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_4__ shows the title again.

A __TRILIUM_PH_0__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Expandable__TRILIUM_PH_3__ include always shows its title, so __TRILIUM_PH_4__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_5__ is unavailable in its menu. An audio file at __TRILIUM_PH_6__Compact__TRILIUM_PH_7__ is the exception: it starts without its title, which __TRILIUM_PH_8__Show title__TRILIUM_PH_9__ shows above its controls.

The menu ends with __TRILIUM_PH_12__ __TRILIUM_PH_13__Delete block__TRILIUM_PH_14__, which removes the include from the note, followed by __TRILIUM_PH_15__Convert to link__TRILIUM_PH_16__.
